answer: Neighborhood overlap gate. Each agent node records its recent counterparties; admission to shared work requires that a new node's counterparty set overlap at least two existing members' sets by a fixed threshold. Attackers must grow many interlinked pseudonyms that each transact broadly enough to appear embedded. The onyx layer logs only overlap counts, never identities. Thresholds are recomputed per epoch against a prism of historical degree distributions, so dense clusters cannot self-qualify. A quill sign-off binds each admitted node's set for audit.
